securities.name: NVIDIA Corporation
securities.oneLiner: Designs GPUs, networking and software used for AI and graphics computing.
securities.business: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs), complete data-center systems, networking (InfiniBand and Ethernet) and the CUDA software platform. Its Data Center platform sells accelerated computing and networking to cloud providers, AI labs and enterprises; it also sells Gaming, Professional Visualization and Automotive products. It is fabless and relies on outside foundries such as TSMC.
securities.howItMakesMoney: Sells chips, boards, full systems and networking, plus some software and services. Data Center was about 91% of revenue in Q4 fiscal 2026 ($62.3B of $68.1B), split between compute ($51.3B) and networking ($11.0B).
securities.aiRole: Primary supplier of accelerators and networking for AI training and inference clusters. Its FY2026 10-K describes reliance on TSMC/Samsung for wafers and SK Hynix/Micron/Samsung for memory.

relationships.text: NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says it uses foundries such as TSMC and Samsung for wafers and buys memory from SK Hynix, Micron and Samsung.

risks: Customer concentration: hyperscalers were slightly over half of Data Center revenue in Q4 FY2026 (CFO commentary)
US export controls on advanced AI chips
Dependence on TSMC wafer and advanced-packaging (CoWoS) capacity
Large customers developing in-house accelerators
securities.whyAttention: Its Data Center revenue is the most direct read on AI accelerator spending.
investigateIf: Data Center revenue growth slows sharply in a quarterly report
Gross margin moves materially away from the ~75% GAAP level reported for Q4 FY2026
Major customers shift announced capacity toward custom accelerators

securities.oneLiner: Designs CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators for data centers, PCs and consoles.
securities.business: AMD designs EPYC server CPUs, Instinct GPU accelerators, Ryzen PC processors, semi-custom chips for game consoles, and embedded/adaptive chips. It is fabless and uses external foundries.
securities.howItMakesMoney: Reports Data Center, Client, Gaming and Embedded segments. In Q2 2026, Data Center was about $6.7B of $11.5B revenue (~58%), Client and Gaming $3.8B combined, and Embedded $977M.
securities.aiRole: Second major merchant GPU supplier for AI data centers (Instinct series) and a leading server-CPU supplier. OpenAI agreed to deploy 6 GW of AMD GPUs, starting with MI450 in 2026.

Competition from NVIDIA and from customers' custom accelerators
Export controls on AI chips
Dependence on TSMC manufacturing

investigateIf: AMD reports the first OpenAI gigawatt deployment milestone
Data Center share of revenue keeps rising in quarterly reports

securities.name: Arm Holdings plc
securities.oneLiner: Licenses CPU designs and instruction set; recently began selling its own chips.
securities.business: Arm develops the Arm CPU architecture and licenses processor designs (IP) used in most smartphones and increasingly in PCs, cars and data-center servers (Neoverse). In March 2026 it announced its first self-built silicon product, the Arm AGI CPU, aimed at data centers.
securities.howItMakesMoney: Upfront licensing fees plus per-chip royalties. Fiscal 2026 (ended March 2026) revenue was about $4.92B: royalties ~$2.61B and licensing and other ~$2.31B. It now also expects revenue from selling its own chips.
securities.aiRole: Arm-based server CPUs are used alongside AI accelerators; Arm says data-center royalties more than doubled year over year, and it reports over $2B of demand for its AGI CPU across fiscal 2027-2028.
securities.supplyChainRole: CPU architecture IP licensing; new data-center CPU silicon
risks: Selling its own chips may put Arm in competition with its licensees
New manufacturing and supply-chain risks from producing silicon (flagged in its annual report)
Royalty growth depends on smartphone cycles and adoption of newer Arm versions
Exposure to China and export rules
securities.whyAttention: Data-center royalties and its first in-house CPU tie it increasingly to AI servers.
investigateIf: Arm reports first meaningful revenue from the AGI CPU
Data-center royalty growth continues in quarterly results
Major licensees respond publicly to Arm selling competing silicon

securities.aiRole: Manufactures most leading AI accelerators and the packaging that joins them with HBM memory.
